purpose: A bounded method for standing up and holding the legal and commercial foundation of a property and casualty agency: establishing the authority to solicit as jurisdiction-specific obligation classes rather than memorized rules (resident and nonresident producer licensing carrying the property and casualty lines of authority, the separate business-entity license and its designated responsible producer, per-carrier per-state appointments, and the recurring filings that keep all of them in force); choosing between captive, independent, franchise and employed-producer operation on the contract terms that actually decide who owns the expirations, what leaving costs and what carrier access the model really delivers; reading commission schedules, direct-bill and agency-bill settlement, return commission and contingency formulas as mechanisms computed from the agency's own contracts and statements rather than as quoted figures; opening carrier access through the path the agency can qualify for and honestly feed - direct appointment, aggregator or cluster membership, franchise, wholesale and managing-general-agent access, or the surplus-lines market - and knowing what each path does to ownership, economics and obligation; carrying errors-and-omissions coverage and delegated binding authority as first-class managed risks; and selecting a market focus across personal and small-commercial lines that the agency's real carrier appetite, service capacity and referral ecosystem can support, all under disclosure-first solicitation conduct so that no consumer is contacted, quoted or bound before the agency is provably licensed, appointed and able to serve them.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is an individual licensed property and casualty producer or a very small independent agency building its own book, not a carrier employee, a managing general agent, a wholesale broker, a claims adjuster or a public adjuster

licensing, entity licensing, appointment, continuing-education, surplus-lines, advertising, rebating and inducement, do-not-call and privacy requirements differ by state, by carrier and by line and change over time, so every such point appears here as an obligation class whose current specifics must be verified with the relevant state insurance department, the carrier's own agency agreement and the agency's counsel before acting

commission rates, contingency formulas, group fee structures, premium volume expectations, startup cost classes and break-even are treated as mechanisms computed from the agency's own carrier schedules, agreements and measured results; no figure in this knowledge base is asserted as a market fact
the durable asset of the agency is the renewal book, so every foundation decision is judged by what it does to owned, renewable, transferable business over years rather than by first-year cash

premium and eligibility are determined by carriers through their own rating, underwriting and filed rules; the agency controls its process, its documentation and where a risk is submitted, never the price or the underwriting outcome
exclusions: risk intake and honest application accuracy, coverage design for auto, home and small-business risks (limits, deductibles, endorsements and exclusions as decision mechanisms), multi-carrier quoting and proposal ethics, and the per-account binding, confirmation-of-coverage and file-documentation discipline for a live placement - that is the quoting, binding and coverage design knowledge base this one hands off to

renewal-cycle management and remarketing decisions, retention economics against new-business economics, claims-time service as the loyalty event, cross-sell and account rounding done from need, and what drives agency book valuation, perpetuation and transferability - that is the renewals, retention and agency book value knowledge base

personalized insurance, financial, legal or tax advice to any consumer or business; this knowledge base is operator education about how a property and casualty agency is licensed, appointed, structured and focused, and any coverage recommendation for a real client follows a documented needs analysis owned by the quoting knowledge base

any solicitation, quoting or binding activity before the individual producer license, the business-entity license where the state requires one, and the applicable carrier appointment are in force; nothing here substitutes for the current requirements published by each state's insurance department

state-specific pre-licensing hours, examination content, fees, fingerprint and background procedures, continuing-education credit counts and renewal cycles, entity-license and responsible-producer rules, appointment filing windows, surplus-lines licensing, tax and stamping duties, broker-fee legality, rebating and inducement limits, and advertising or do-not-call specifics, all of which appear only as obligation classes to verify in the operating jurisdiction

specific commission percentages, contingency payouts, aggregator or franchise fee levels, premium volume thresholds, account counts, startup cost amounts, revenue-per-account figures or book multiples; compensation and cost appear only as mechanisms to compute from the agency's own contracts, statements and measured results

any promise, projection or implication that a consumer will save money, that a quote will hold, or that coverage is in force before the carrier has confirmed it; premium and eligibility are carrier-determined
claims adjusting, coverage determination and claim-denial advocacy, which are separate licensed functions belonging to adjusters, public adjusters or attorneys
life, health, Medicare, annuity and employee-benefits lines and any securities or investment-advisory activity, each of which requires its own license and belongs to a different practice
carrier-side and program work: rate and form filing, underwriting authority beyond a delegated binding grant, managing-general-agent and program administration, and reinsurance

competency_questions.question: What exactly must be in force - for me personally, for my agency entity, and for each carrier - before I may quote or bind a single property or casualty policy, and how do I prove on any given day that it still is?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PC_LICENSE_PATH gives the individual licensing requirement classes and the evidence artifact each produces, ENTITY_LICENSE_AND_DRLP separates the entity credential and its responsible producer from the individual license, CARRIER_APPOINTMENT_MECHANICS separates the appointment from the license and names the authority register checked before each case, and AGENCY_READINESS_GATE states the full pass condition set

competency_questions.question: Which recurring obligations keep my licenses, appointments and errors-and-omissions coverage alive, who owns each one, and what actually breaks when one lapses?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTINUING_OBLIGATIONS_CALENDAR enumerates the recurring obligation classes with owner, cadence, lead time and evidence artifact and states the consequence class of a lapse for pending business and compensation, and EO_PROGRAM_POSTURE explains why coverage continuity is itself a recurring obligation

competency_questions.question: What do I do when a risk sits in a state I am not licensed in, or in a class none of my carriers will write?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NONRESIDENT_FOOTPRINT states that authority follows where the risk and transaction sit and gives the nonresident, home-state and surplus-lines mechanisms, AGENCY_SCOPE_CHARTER supplies the refusal list with a named referral home, and CARRIER_ACCESS_PATHS gives the wholesale and surplus-lines route for classes the shelf cannot write

competency_questions.question: Captive, independent, franchise, or producing inside someone else's agency - which model should I operate under, and which contract terms decide it rather than which pitch sounds best?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AFFILIATION_MODEL_COMPARISON compares the models as contract structures on the four durable axes of relationship ownership, exit cost, real carrier access and priced value of bundled support, and BOOK_OWNERSHIP_TERMS supplies the clause-level evidence each axis is answered from

competency_questions.question: Who owns the renewals if I leave, or if the carrier or group terminates the agreement, and what do the ownership-of-expirations and restrictive-covenant clauses actually do to me?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_OWNERSHIP_TERMS defines ownership of expirations and the termination, run-off, covenant and assignment clauses that travel with it, AGGREGATOR_CLUSTER_TERMS states what group membership does to that ownership, and AFFILIATION_MODEL_COMPARISON places the answer in the model choice

competency_questions.question: How does money actually arrive from a bound policy - how is commission computed, when is it paid, when is it taken back, and how does direct bill differ from agency bill?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMISSION_STRUCTURE_MECHANICS describes the rate, the premium base, the settlement path with its fiduciary duty over agency-bill funds, and return commission on cancellation and downward endorsement, all as mechanisms read from the agency's own schedules and statements

competency_questions.question: What is contingency or profit-sharing income, what actually moves it, and how do I keep it from deciding where I place a client?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTINGENCY_INCOME_MECHANICS gives the volume, growth, retention and loss-ratio inputs, the timing and volatility that keep it out of the cost budget, and COMPENSATION_CONFLICT_DISCLOSURE gives the procedural resolution that places business on documented fit with the reason recorded

competency_questions.question: No carrier will appoint a brand-new agency directly for the markets I need - what are the real access paths, and what does each one cost me in ownership and economics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARRIER_ACCESS_PATHS distinguishes direct appointment, aggregator or cluster, franchise, wholesale and managing-general-agent, and surplus-lines access as mechanisms and evaluates each on qualification, cost, ownership effect and obligation created, and AGGREGATOR_CLUSTER_TERMS supplies the term-level detail for the group path

competency_questions.question: What must I extract from an aggregator, cluster, network or franchise agreement before I sign it, and what would make me walk away?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AGGREGATOR_CLUSTER_TERMS lists the fee and value-extraction structure, whose name the appointments carry, ownership of expirations and the exit mechanics, and production minimums, and BOOK_OWNERSHIP_TERMS supplies the ownership test the agreement must pass

competency_questions.question: How many carriers should I actually carry, how do I keep an appointment from being restricted or terminated, and what happens to my book if one is put in run-off?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VOLUME_COMMITMENT_MANAGEMENT names the metrics carriers judge an appointment by, the escalation path from warning to termination, and the concentration limit the agency writes down, and CARRIER_APPOINTMENT_MECHANICS supplies the agreement terms and register those decisions are read from

competency_questions.question: How long must I fund this agency before commission covers cost, and what mechanism decides the answer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AGENCY_CAPITALIZATION_RUNWAY names the cost classes and the timing mechanism by which commission lags cost and renewals compound later, COMMISSION_STRUCTURE_MECHANICS supplies the settlement and reversal behaviour the model runs on, and LINE_ECONOMICS_SERVICE_LOAD supplies the per-line yield and capacity inputs

competency_questions.question: Should I build this agency on personal lines or small commercial, and how do I test that choice against the carriers I can actually access and the service load I can actually carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_FOCUS_SELECTION contrasts the two segments as different businesses and gives the four assessment criteria, LINE_ECONOMICS_SERVICE_LOAD supplies the measured yield, touch-count and exposure comparison, and NICHE_APPETITE_ALIGNMENT tests the chosen class against real carrier appetite

competency_questions.question: Where do property and casualty accounts actually come from, and what are the conduct limits on how I get them and what I may pay for them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REFERRAL_SOURCE_ARCHITECTURE names the channel classes and the rebating, inducement, settlement-service referral, consent and privacy obligation classes each must clear, and SOLICITATION_ETHICS_DISCLOSURE supplies the disclosure-first standard every channel's contact must meet

competency_questions.question: What am I allowed to bind on my own authority, what must go to an underwriter first, and how do I keep the errors-and-omissions exposure of that boundary managed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BINDING_AUTHORITY_LIMITS states the per-carrier grant by line, class, limit and condition, the prohibited classes and suspension events, and the documented referral route, and EO_PROGRAM_POSTURE explains why acting outside the grant is the least defensible exposure the agency can create

glossary.definition: The class of insurance a producer license permits its holder to transact - in this domain property and casualty, which some states issue as separate property and casualty lines, some as a combined credential, and some alongside a narrower personal-lines-only authority; the exact division and naming is set by each state.

A carrier's filed authorization for a specific licensed producer or agency to solicit and submit business for that carrier in a specific state. It is separate from the license, is created by the agency agreement behind it, and can be terminated by the carrier while the license remains perfectly valid.

The contractual right to the policy and customer expiration information that lets its holder approach the client at renewal. It is the clause that decides whether a renewal book is the agency's asset or the carrier's, and it is conditioned or forfeited in many captive, franchise, cluster and employed-producer agreements.

Authority delegated in an agency agreement to put coverage in force on the carrier's behalf, granted narrowly by line, class, limit and condition, with prohibited classes and events such as catastrophe moratoriums that suspend it entirely.

Two premium settlement mechanisms. Under direct bill the carrier bills the client and remits commission on a statement cycle; under agency bill the agency invoices the client, collects the premium and remits it net of commission under an account-current, holding money that is not its own.

Variable back-end compensation a carrier pays after a measurement period closes, computed on a formula the carrier sets and can change - typically premium volume, growth, retention and above all loss ratio - and therefore never budgetable as current revenue.

A group mechanism through which independent agencies pool premium volume so that carriers which would decline each member individually will appoint the group, in exchange for fees, a share of commission, or both, and with consequences for whose name the appointments carry.

Placement with carriers not admitted in the state, used for risks the admitted market declines. It requires its own license class, a documented diligent search of admitted markets, and premium tax and stamping duties, and it carries no state guaranty-fund protection for the insured.

Professional liability protecting the agency against allegations that it failed in placing or servicing coverage. It is typically written on a claims-made basis, so the retroactive date, continuity across carrier changes, prior-acts coverage and tail coverage at sale or wind-down decide whether past work stays defended.

Incurred losses measured against earned premium on the business an agency places with a carrier. It is the number the carrier uses to judge whether an appointment is worth keeping, and it is the dominant input to most contingency formulas.

nodes.definition: Write down, before anything is licensed or contracted, what this agency sells, what it refuses, and where refused business goes. A property and casualty agency can touch personal auto, homeowners, renters, condominium, landlord and umbrella coverage as well as small-commercial lines such as business owners policies, general liability, commercial auto and workers compensation, and each of those is a decision to carry rather than an accident of whoever calls. The charter also names the classes the agency will not touch without a specialist - large or hazardous commercial risks, professional liability that belongs with a specialty broker, flood and earthquake where a separate program applies, life, health and benefits lines that require other licenses, and any risk that must go to the surplus-lines market - and it names the person or firm each refusal is referred to. It states the standing language every consumer conversation carries: that this is a licensed insurance agency and not a source of legal, tax or financial advice, that premium and eligibility are set by carriers, and that no savings are promised. The charter is the document every later decision is tested against, so that when a carrier, a group or a lead vendor asks the agency to write something outside it, the answer is fast and already reasoned.

included: the lines and account classes the agency intends to write
the explicit refusal list with a named referral home for each refusal
the standing educational and no-guarantee language used in every consumer conversation
the test that later carrier, group and marketing decisions are checked against
excluded: designing coverage or recommending limits for any specific client, which follows a documented needs analysis in the quoting knowledge base
book valuation and perpetuation planning, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the agency changes the lines it writes or the classes it refuses, or a referral home for a refusal class changes

pros.claim: A written refusal list turns out-of-appetite and out-of-license business into a same-day referral instead of a slow and dangerous attempt
pros.example: a prospect with a forty-unit apartment schedule and prior water losses is referred to a commercial specialist immediately rather than shopped for three weeks and placed badly

cons.claim: A charter written before the agency has met its market can exclude the very accounts that turn out to be its best niche
cons.example: refusing all contractor risks at the outset in a territory where small trade contractors are the densest referral source

failure_modes: writing the charter as marketing language rather than an operating boundary that actually refuses business
leaving a refusal class with no named referral home, so refusals become abandoned prospects
letting the charter drift silently as the agency chases whatever quote requests arrive
acceptance_tests: the charter names the lines written, at least three refusal classes each with a named referral home, and the standing no-advice and carrier-determined-premium sentences, and every marketing asset in use matches it
revisit_triggers: a class of business the market keeps presenting is refused repeatedly within a quarter
a carrier or group relationship changes what the agency can honestly write
a referral partner for a refusal class is added or lost

nodes.definition: Obtain and keep the individual producer license carrying the property and casualty lines of authority in the resident state, treated as a sequence of requirement classes rather than a memorized checklist, because every specific inside it is set by that state's insurance department and changes. The classes that recur across states are a pre-licensing education requirement tied to each line of authority; a proctored examination per line, sometimes split between property and casualty and sometimes offered as a combined credential; an application with fees; a background component that commonly includes fingerprinting and disclosure of criminal, regulatory and financial history; and in some states a sponsorship or an appointment filed before the license becomes fully usable. Several states also issue a narrower personal-lines-only credential, which changes what the licensee may lawfully write. Each completed class leaves an artifact - a course completion certificate, an examination result, a license number with an expiration date, a background clearance - and those artifacts, not memory, are what a carrier's contracting packet and a regulator's inquiry ask for. Current requirements, their order and their processing times are verified with the state insurance department before starting, never assumed from another state's process or from a forum answer.

included: the requirement classes that produce an individual resident license with property and casualty lines of authority
the evidence artifact each class produces and where it is filed
the difference between a personal-lines-only credential and full property and casualty authority
verification of current specifics with the state insurance department before acting
excluded: state-specific hours, fees, examination content and processing times, which are verified in the operating jurisdiction rather than asserted here
the business-entity license, which is a separate credential
carrier appointments, which are a separate authority from the license

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the resident state changes a licensing requirement class, or the license status or expiration changes

pros.claim: Treating licensing as requirement classes with artifacts makes the same method work in any state and survives rule changes
pros.example: an agent expanding into a second state runs the same class list - education, examination, application, background, sponsorship - and re-verifies each specific with that state's department

cons.claim: Requirement classes cannot say what a given state requires today, so the method always carries a verification step that costs time before any move
cons.example: a planned launch date slipping because fingerprint appointments and license issuance in that state take longer than assumed

failure_modes: soliciting or quoting while the license application is still pending
holding a personal-lines-only credential and quoting a commercial risk the authority does not cover
letting the license expire because the renewal cycle was never entered into a calendar with lead time
acceptance_tests: the license record shows the property and casualty lines of authority active with its number and expiration date, and every requirement class in the state's current publication has a matching filed artifact
revisit_triggers: the state publishes a change to licensing, examination or background requirements
the agency intends to write a line the current lines of authority do not cover

nodes.definition: Decide and maintain the set of states the agency can lawfully write in, on the rule that authority follows where the risk and the transaction sit rather than where the client happens to live or call from. Property and casualty work produces cross-border situations constantly: a client who moves, a rental house two states away, a contractor working across a state line, a fleet garaged elsewhere, a second home on the coast. The mechanisms to hold are the nonresident producer license, usually issued on the strength of an active resident license through a reciprocity class rather than by re-examination; the home-state designation that determines which state's rules govern the producer; the requirement that the carrier also be authorized and appointed in that state, because the producer's license alone is not enough; and the surplus-lines credential, which is its own license class carrying diligent-search documentation, premium tax and stamping duties when no admitted market will take the risk. Nonresident licenses cost money and interact with renewal and continuing-education obligations, so the footprint is chosen deliberately as the states the agency actually serves rather than collected. When a risk falls outside the footprint, the answer is a recorded referral to a producer licensed there, not an attempt to write it from here.

included: the nonresident licensing and reciprocity mechanism and the home-state concept
the rule that authority is decided by where the risk and the transaction sit
surplus lines as a separate license class with diligent-search, tax and stamping duties
the deliberate choice of footprint and the recorded referral path for out-of-footprint risks
excluded: each state's specific nonresident fees, reciprocity conditions and stamping mechanics, which are verified with that state's department and stamping office
coverage design for out-of-state exposures, which the quoting knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a state is added to or removed from the served footprint, or a state changes nonresident or surplus-lines requirements

pros.claim: A defined footprint turns every cross-border question into a lookup and a clean referral instead of an improvised decision under deadline
pros.example: a long-standing auto client buys a cabin across the state line and the agency knows immediately whether it can write it or must refer

cons.claim: Every added state multiplies renewal, education and appointment maintenance for volume that may never justify it
cons.example: a nonresident license obtained for one relocating household that produces a single policy and then renews for years

failure_modes: quoting a risk located in a state where either the producer or the carrier lacks authority
assuming reciprocity is automatic and skipping the nonresident application entirely
placing surplus-lines business without the surplus-lines credential or the diligent-search record
acceptance_tests: every state in the footprint has an active resident or nonresident license on file with its expiration, and out-of-footprint risks in the last period show a recorded referral rather than a quote
revisit_triggers: a client relocates or acquires property or operations in a new state
a state changes reciprocity, nonresident or surplus-lines requirements
the agency decides to add or drop a state from the served footprint

nodes.definition: License the agency itself, not only the person inside it. In most states the firm - corporation, limited liability company or partnership - holds its own business-entity producer license distinct from the individual licenses of its people, and that entity license names a designated responsible licensed producer who is personally accountable to the regulator for the entity's compliance, supervision and records. This matters commercially because carrier agency agreements, appointment filings, commission payments and errors-and-omissions policies attach to the entity rather than to a human being: an agency operating on an individual license alone can find that its carrier contracts, its book and its liability all sit on one person and cannot be transferred. The related classes to settle at the same time are trade-name or assumed-name registration and, where required, its approval so the name used in advertising matches the licensed name; the ownership and officer disclosures the entity application requires; and the supervision structure that records who reviews the work of unlicensed staff, since clerical employees may take information but soliciting, negotiating and binding are licensed acts. Whether an entity license is required at all, who may serve as responsible producer and how name approval works are verified with each state's department before the agency signs its first carrier agreement.

included: the business-entity producer license as a credential separate from the individual license
the designated responsible producer role and the supervision boundary over unlicensed staff
trade-name registration and name-use consistency across advertising
the fact that carrier agreements, appointments, commissions and errors-and-omissions coverage attach to the licensed entity
excluded: choice of legal entity form and its tax treatment, which belong to the agency's attorney and accountant
specific state entity-license fees, forms and name-approval procedures, which are verified in the operating jurisdiction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the entity's ownership, responsible producer, trade name or licensed states change

pros.claim: Putting contracts, commissions and coverage on a licensed entity separates the agency as an asset from the individual and is what makes a book transferable later
pros.example: a carrier agreement and its commission stream sit with the agency, so adding a partner or selling later does not require every contract to be re-papered out of a personal name

cons.claim: The entity layer adds its own license, renewal, name-approval and reporting obligations a solo producer would not otherwise carry
cons.example: a second renewal cycle and a second set of filings to track for a one-person agency writing modest volume

failure_modes: operating under a trade name that was never registered or approved for insurance use
letting unlicensed staff solicit or bind because the supervision boundary was never written down
leaving a stale designated responsible producer on file after the named person's role has changed
acceptance_tests: the entity license is active with its number and expiration, the designated responsible producer on file is the person actually performing that role, and the advertising name matches the licensed or registered name
revisit_triggers: ownership, officers or the designated responsible producer change
the agency adds staff who will touch consumer conversations
a state changes entity-licensing or name-approval rules

nodes.definition: Build one calendar holding every recurring obligation that keeps the agency's authority and protection alive, each with an owner, a cadence, a lead time and the artifact that proves it was done. The obligation classes in a property and casualty agency are continuing-education credits and license renewal for each individual license in each state; entity-license renewal; appointment maintenance, including carriers that terminate appointments for inactivity and states that require renewal filings; errors-and-omissions renewal with attention to continuity of the retroactive date; surplus-lines tax and stamping filings where that credential is held; carrier-required annual attestations, product certifications and system access recertifications; and privacy, records-retention and do-not-call obligations that run continuously rather than annually. The calendar's real value is its lead time, because an item entered on its due date is already late: education takes weeks, background and processing take longer, and a carrier's contracting queue is not the agency's to schedule. The consequence class of a lapse is why it is run this way - pending business can be voided, compensation on business written without authority can be forfeited or clawed back, an appointment can terminate, and the lapse itself is usually reportable on every future application and contracting packet.

included: every recurring licensing, appointment, coverage, filing and carrier obligation with owner, cadence, lead time and evidence artifact
the consequence class of a lapse for pending business, in-force compensation and future contracting
lead times sized to absorb a busy month or a storm season
excluded: state-specific credit counts, renewal cycles and filing deadlines, which are verified with each department and carrier
the per-account renewal service calendar, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an obligation changes cadence or content, a credential is added, or a lapse occurs

pros.claim: One calendar with lead times converts a set of silent expiry risks into scheduled work that is completed early and evidenced
pros.example: education credits completed a full cycle ahead of the renewal date so a heavy storm season never collides with a license deadline

cons.claim: Maintenance consumes producer time that generates no revenue and is the first thing dropped when the agency gets busy
cons.example: the quarter the agency doubles quote volume is exactly the quarter a carrier attestation goes unanswered

failure_modes: treating the renewal date as the deadline rather than the completion date
tracking the individual license while forgetting entity renewal, appointment maintenance or the errors-and-omissions renewal
letting an appointment lapse for inactivity and discovering it when a submission is rejected
acceptance_tests: every license, appointment, coverage and filing obligation in force appears in the calendar with an owner, a lead time and its most recent evidence artifact, and no item has passed its lead-time start with no work begun
revisit_triggers: a state, carrier or errors-and-omissions condition changes an obligation's cadence or content
a new state, carrier or credential is added
an obligation is missed or completed late

nodes.definition: A license permits a person or entity to transact insurance; a carrier appointment is the separate authority to represent that specific carrier in that specific state, and the agency agreement behind it is the contract that actually defines the relationship. Both must be in force at the moment of solicitation, and they fail independently - a perfectly valid license does nothing for a carrier whose appointment was terminated for inactivity. Contracting is effectively an underwriting of the agency: the packet asks for licensing evidence, the entity license, proof of errors-and-omissions coverage at the carrier's required limit, ownership and background disclosures, prior terminations and unpaid agent balances, and often a business plan with projected volume, plus a check of industry databases that surface past terminations for cause. States differ on whether the appointment must be filed before the first application or within a defined window after it, and carriers differ in how they handle that, so the rule is verified per carrier and per state rather than generalized from one relationship. What the work produces is an authority register: for every carrier and state, appointment status with effective and termination dates, the agreement's key terms by reference, the binding grant, and the termination provisions - consulted before a case rather than remembered.

included: appointment as per-carrier and per-state authority distinct from licensure
the contracting packet and the agency-underwriting checks it triggers
the authority register with effective dates and the pre-case lookup
termination provisions, including termination for cause and its reporting class
excluded: the commission schedule inside the same agreement, read as its own work unit
ownership of expirations and restrictive covenants, abstracted separately before signing
the per-policy binding process for a live account, which the quoting and binding knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an appointment status, agency agreement term, or a state's appointment filing rule changes

pros.claim: An authority register makes the pre-quote check a lookup across many carriers and states instead of a memory exercise
pros.example: before quoting a commercial auto risk garaged in a second state, the agency confirms in one place that the carrier is appointed there and the agreement covers that line

cons.claim: Contracting is slow, front-loaded and largely outside the agency's control, so the register is thinnest exactly when a new opportunity arrives
cons.example: a referred restaurant package needs a carrier the agency is not yet contracted with, and the contracting queue outlasts the client's renewal date

failure_modes: assuming a license alone permits writing a given carrier's product
omitting a prior termination or unpaid balance on the contracting disclosure and having the agreement voided later
learning that an appointment was terminated only when a submission is rejected
acceptance_tests: for every carrier and state the agency intends to write, the register shows an in-force appointment or a verified just-in-time rule with its window, current errors-and-omissions evidence at the carrier's required limit, and the agreement's termination provision recorded
revisit_triggers: a carrier terminates, suspends or declines to renew an appointment
the agency adds a carrier or a state
an agency agreement is amended or re-papered through a different group

nodes.definition: Read out of each agency agreement exactly what the agency may put in force on the carrier's behalf and what must go to an underwriter first, then keep that boundary somewhere a producer can see it while a client is on the phone. Delegated binding authority in property and casualty is granted narrowly and conditionally: by line and class, by limit and coverage amount, by construction, occupancy, protection class or driver characteristics, by prior-loss history, and with named prohibited classes the agency may never bind. Layered on top are the events that suspend authority entirely - catastrophe moratoriums when a named storm enters a watch area or a wildfire is burning, blackout windows around effective dates, and any risk the carrier's system flags for referral. The costly asymmetry is that binding beyond authority does not simply fail quietly: the client believes coverage is in place, the carrier may decline to honour a placement the agency had no authority to make, and the gap lands on the agency as an errors-and-omissions matter. The discipline is therefore to bind only inside the written grant, to route everything else as a referral with the request and the response documented, and to tell the client plainly that coverage is not in force until the carrier confirms it.

included: the per-carrier grant of binding authority by line, class, limit and condition
prohibited classes and the events that suspend authority, including catastrophe moratoriums
the referral route for risks outside authority and the documentation it produces
the standing rule that a client is told coverage is not in force until the carrier confirms it
excluded: the per-account binding checklist, confirmation-of-coverage wording and file documentation for a live placement, which the quoting and binding knowledge base owns
coverage design and limit selection for a specific risk

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier changes its binding grant, prohibited classes or moratorium posture

pros.claim: A visible authority boundary lets the agency say yes instantly where it truly can and route everything else without guessing
pros.example: a homeowners risk inside the carrier's construction and prior-loss parameters is bound on the spot while a coastal risk under a named-storm watch is routed to the underwriter with the request logged

cons.claim: Narrow authority slows the agency exactly where speed wins accounts, and every referral adds turnaround a competitor may not have
cons.example: a small contractor with one prior claim needs underwriter review while a competing agency with a broader grant binds the same day

failure_modes: binding a prohibited class because the carrier's system happened to allow the transaction
issuing anything a client could read as confirmation of coverage before the carrier has confirmed it
ignoring a moratorium because the risk was already quoted before it started
acceptance_tests: each carrier's binding grant, prohibited classes and suspension conditions are recorded in one place, and every placement in the period was either inside that grant or shows a documented underwriter referral and response
revisit_triggers: a carrier amends its binding grant or issues a moratorium
an errors-and-omissions claim or near-miss involves an authority question
a new line or class is added to what the agency writes

nodes.definition: Treat errors-and-omissions coverage as an asset the agency manages rather than a box a carrier makes it tick. This coverage responds to allegations that the agency failed in placing or servicing insurance - the endorsement never added, the higher limit never offered, the flood or umbrella conversation never had, the renewal never remarketed - and in property and casualty those allegations arrive years later, at the moment of a large claim, from a client who is already unhappy. The mechanics that matter are structural. These policies are typically claims-made, so the retroactive date and continuity of coverage across renewals and carrier changes decide whether past work is still defended; limits and deductibles interact with what each carrier agency agreement requires the agency to carry; prior-acts coverage and, at sale or wind-down, tail coverage determine what happens to historic placements; and the application itself asks what the agency writes, so a change in the mix of business is a disclosure event rather than a private decision. Alongside the policy sits the loss-control half: written documentation habits, signed coverage rejections, proposals that record what was offered and declined, and refusal to work outside binding authority. Premium is set by the errors-and-omissions carrier from the agency's own profile, and no cost figure is asserted here.

included: errors-and-omissions coverage as claims-made professional liability with retroactive date, prior acts and tail considerations
the interaction between agency-agreement requirements and the limits actually carried
disclosure duties when the agency's mix of business changes
the documentation and refusal habits that function as loss control
excluded: the per-file documentation standard for a live account, which the quoting and binding knowledge base owns
claims-time client service and advocacy, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns
any specific premium, limit or deductible figure, which the errors-and-omissions carrier sets from the agency's own profile

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the program's retroactive date, limits or carrier changes, or the disclosed composition of the book changes

pros.claim: Managing the retroactive date and prior-acts continuity keeps years of past placements defended even as coverage carriers change
pros.example: switching errors-and-omissions carriers with the original retroactive date preserved rather than reset, so a claim on a policy placed three years earlier is still within coverage

cons.claim: The coverage is a real fixed cost carried from before the first placement, when there is no revenue and the exposure still feels theoretical
cons.example: binding coverage as a condition of a carrier contracting packet months before the first commission statement arrives

failure_modes: changing carriers and accepting a new retroactive date, silently stranding prior work
letting coverage lapse between carriers and creating a gap no later policy will pick up
answering the application from an outdated picture of what the agency now writes
acceptance_tests: the policy is in force with its retroactive date, limit and deductible recorded, the limit meets or exceeds every current agency agreement's requirement, and the classes written match what was disclosed on the application
revisit_triggers: the agency adds a line, class or state materially different from what was disclosed
a renewal, carrier change or claim occurs on the errors-and-omissions program
a carrier agreement raises its required limit

nodes.definition: Choose how the agency will exist, on the terms that outlive the pitch. The realistic models are the captive or exclusive agency, where one carrier supplies brand, training, systems and often an early subsidy while restricting the agency to that carrier's products and frequently holding or conditioning the customer relationship; the independent agency, which contracts with multiple carriers, normally owns its expirations and carries every cost itself; the franchise or branded network, which sells a system, carrier access and support for fees and a share of commission; and producing inside someone else's agency as an employee or contract producer, trading ownership for a salary or a split with no capital at risk. Four axes actually decide the choice: who owns the renewals, what leaving costs and how long it takes, what carrier access the model really delivers for the intended market in this territory, and what the bundled support is worth when priced against buying the same services directly. Early subsidy, signing incentives and headline split talk are the least durable terms in any of these arrangements and belong last in the weighting. The output is a written decision against those four axes, each answer supported by the specific clause it came from, with at least one rejected alternative recorded.

included: captive, independent, franchise and employed-producer operation compared as contract structures
the four durable axes of relationship ownership, exit cost, real carrier access and priced value of bundled support
the rule that subsidies and headline splits are weighted last
the written decision with supporting clause references and a recorded rejected alternative
excluded: what an assembled book is worth and how it is sold or perpetuated, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns
any specific commission split, fee level or subsidy amount, which comes only from the agreement offered

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a model's contract terms, carrier access in the territory, or the priced value of its support package changes materially

pros.claim: Deciding on ownership, exit, access and priced support keeps the choice from turning on a recruiting number that expires within a year
pros.example: an offer with a visibly better split is declined once the exit provision shows the renewals stay behind on any departure

cons.claim: The durable axes are hardest to evaluate exactly when the operator has least leverage and least experience reading agency agreements
cons.example: a first-time agency owner signing before an attorney has read the termination and non-solicitation language

failure_modes: choosing on the training and subsidy promised in the first year
assuming multi-carrier access without checking which carriers the model actually delivers in this territory
not knowing at signing who owns the client if the relationship ends
acceptance_tests: the chosen model is written down with the contract clause that answers each of the four axes, and at least one rejected alternative is recorded with the reason it was rejected
revisit_triggers: the carrier or group changes ownership, compensation or termination terms
the intended market needs carriers the current model cannot deliver
the bundled support is measured to cost more than buying the same services directly

nodes.definition: Find, read and abstract the clauses that decide whether the renewals the agency writes are its property. In property and casualty the governing concept is ownership of expirations: the right to the policy and customer expiration information that lets whoever holds it approach the client at renewal. In an independent agency agreement that right normally sits with the agency and is the reason a book is an asset at all; in captive, franchise, cluster and employed-producer arrangements it is frequently conditioned, shared or forfeited on termination, sometimes only for cause and sometimes on any termination whatsoever. The related clauses travel together and are read as a set: termination with and without cause and the notice each requires; whether the book goes into run-off with the agency still servicing and earning or transfers immediately; non-solicitation, non-piracy and non-compete covenants with their duration and geography; any buy-back or purchase right and the formula behind it; and assignment provisions deciding whether the book can be sold or moved at all. The abstract is written before signing, because none of these clauses are negotiable afterwards and every one of them is what a buyer, a lender or a successor will eventually examine.

included: ownership of expirations as the clause that makes renewals an asset
termination with and without cause, notice periods, and run-off versus immediate transfer
non-solicitation, non-piracy, non-compete and assignment provisions
the written clause abstract produced before signing
excluded: valuing the book, computing a multiple or structuring a sale or perpetuation, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns
the commission schedule's rates and settlement terms, which are read as their own work unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an agreement's ownership, termination, covenant or assignment language changes, or the counterparty changes

pros.claim: Knowing before signing who owns the expirations decides whether years of renewal work build an asset or rent one
pros.example: an agreement that returns expirations to the carrier on any termination is recognized as building the carrier's book rather than the agency's

cons.claim: Ownership-friendly terms usually come with less support, less capital and harder carrier access, so insisting on them carries a real price
cons.example: declining a franchise's ready-made market access because its exit provisions condition the renewals

failure_modes: signing without reading the termination and covenant clauses because a recruiter described them
assuming an independent contract automatically means clean ownership without checking assignment and covenant language
discovering a non-solicitation radius or duration only when planning to leave
acceptance_tests: for every carrier, group or employment agreement in force, a written abstract states who owns expirations, what happens on termination with and without cause, the covenant terms and duration, and whether the book may be assigned
revisit_triggers: any agreement is signed, amended, assigned or re-papered
a carrier or group is acquired and the contract moves to a new counterparty
the agency contemplates adding a partner, selling, or leaving a group

nodes.definition: Understand the machine that turns a bound policy into money, because every economic decision downstream depends on its timing far more than on any headline rate. The mechanism has four parts. The rate: the agency agreement's commission schedule sets a percentage of premium that differs by line, by new versus renewal business, and sometimes by state or program, and it is read from the schedule rather than assumed from what another agency reports. The base: commission is computed on premium as written or as collected depending on the arrangement, so endorsements, cancellations and audits on commercial policies move it after the fact. The settlement path: under direct bill the carrier bills the client and remits commission on a statement cycle, while under agency bill the agency invoices, collects and remits net premium under an account-current, holding money that belongs to the carrier and the client under fiduciary duties. And reversal: cancellations, flat cancels and downward endorsements produce return commission netted from later statements, so revenue recognized early can be taken back. The agency models all four parts from its own schedules and reconciled statements; no rate, split or amount is credible here except the one printed in its own contract.

included: the commission-rate mechanism and where the schedule lives in the agreement
written versus collected premium as the base, and how endorsements, cancellations and audits move it
direct bill versus agency bill settlement and the fiduciary duty over agency-bill funds
return commission and chargeback on cancellation and downward endorsement
excluded: contingency and profit-sharing income, which is a separate mechanism with different behaviour
any specific commission percentage or amount, which comes only from the agency's own carrier schedules
retention economics and the compounding value of renewal commission over years, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier commission schedule, billing arrangement or observed statement behaviour changes

pros.claim: Modelling timing and reversal rather than rates shows what the agency will actually hold after a normal month of endorsements and cancellations
pros.example: a strong new-business month that nets low once two flat cancels and a downward auto endorsement reverse earlier commission

cons.claim: The mechanism is only fully knowable from statements that arrive after the fact, so early planning runs on estimates that cannot yet be verified
cons.example: a first-year budget built before a full statement cycle has shown how one carrier handles mid-term changes and audits

failure_modes: treating written-premium commission as cash before the statement clears
spending agency-bill collections that are premium held for the carrier rather than agency revenue
budgeting from a headline new-business rate while most of the book renews at a different one
acceptance_tests: for each carrier the schedule's new and renewal rate by line, the commission base, the settlement path and the return-commission treatment are recorded, and at least one full statement cycle has been reconciled against them
revisit_triggers: a carrier amends its commission schedule or settlement terms
statements stop reconciling to the recorded mechanism
the agency's mix shifts toward a line with a different rate structure

nodes.definition: Contingent commission, profit sharing and growth bonuses form a second income stream that behaves nothing like base commission, and treating the two as the same thing is how small agencies get into trouble. The mechanism: a carrier measures the book the agency places with it over a defined period - premium volume, growth against the prior period, retention, and above all loss ratio, meaning incurred losses against earned premium - and pays a variable amount after the period closes, under a formula in a schedule the carrier can revise or withdraw. Three properties follow from that. It is back-end and late, arriving after the year it was earned in, so it can never fund current fixed costs. It is volatile, because one severe fire or liability claim inside a small book can erase a year's contingency, which means a small agency sees far more variance than a large one. And it is an incentive pointed straight at the client file: a formula rewarding low loss ratio quietly rewards shedding riskier clients, and one rewarding volume rewards steering placements toward a single carrier. The agency's response is to model contingency from its own carrier schedules as an uncertain bonus, never as budgeted revenue, and to place business on documented client fit so the formula never decides where an account goes.

included: the volume, growth, retention and loss-ratio inputs that produce contingency
its timing and volatility, and why a small book sees more variance
the placement and client-selection incentives the formula creates and how they are neutralized
modelling it from the agency's own carrier schedules as an uncertain bonus
excluded: any specific contingency rate, threshold or payout amount
base commission mechanics, which are their own work unit
the client-facing coverage recommendation itself, which the quoting knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier's contingency schedule changes, or the agency's loss-ratio position with that carrier moves materially

pros.claim: Understanding the formula shows which of the agency's own behaviours actually move it and which are noise
pros.example: recognizing that a single severe claim rather than a slow growth month is what removed a year's contingency from a small book

cons.claim: The formula is set, revised and withdrawn by the carrier and is opaque in its details, so even a careful model stays an estimate the agency cannot control
cons.example: a schedule restructured mid-period so the growth component the agency had been tracking no longer applies

failure_modes: budgeting contingency into fixed costs and being short when a loss year zeroes it
letting the loss-ratio incentive quietly change which clients the agency accepts or keeps
steering placements toward the carrier whose volume threshold is nearly met
acceptance_tests: each carrier's contingency inputs and measurement period are recorded from its own schedule, no contingency amount appears in the agency's committed cost budget, and placement records justify carrier choice by client fit rather than by threshold position
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes or withdraws its contingency schedule
a large claim materially moves loss ratio with a carrier
a placement decision is questioned as threshold-driven

nodes.definition: Solve the founding problem of an independent property and casualty agency: the carriers its market needs will often not appoint a brand-new agency directly, because a direct appointment is a bet on premium volume, loss ratio and staying power that a new agency cannot yet evidence. The available paths are distinct mechanisms rather than synonyms. A direct appointment is a bilateral agency agreement with the carrier - best economics, cleanest ownership, hardest to obtain, and usually conditioned on experience, a business plan, projected volume and the carrier's own need in that territory. Aggregators, clusters and networks pool many small agencies so the group's aggregate volume satisfies carriers that would decline each member alone, in exchange for fees, a share of commission, or both. A franchise sells access bundled with brand and systems. Wholesale brokers, managing general agents and program administrators supply access per placement with no appointment at all, taking a share of the commission and usually holding the carrier relationship themselves. Surplus-lines brokers place what the admitted market declines, under a separate license class. The realistic answer is usually a combination sequenced over time, and every path is evaluated on four questions: what it requires to qualify, what it costs in fees and commission share, what it does to ownership of the expirations, and what obligation it creates back to the carrier or group.

included: direct appointment, aggregator or cluster, franchise, wholesale and managing-general-agent, and surplus-lines access as distinct mechanisms
the qualification requirements each imposes on a new agency
the four evaluation questions of qualification, cost, ownership effect and obligation created
sequencing paths over time as the agency builds a volume and performance record
excluded: the specific terms of any one group agreement, which are abstracted in their own work unit
specific fee levels, splits or volume thresholds, which come only from the agreements actually offered
product and coverage selection for a client's risk, which the quoting knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: carrier appointment availability in the territory changes, or the agency's qualification profile changes

pros.claim: Naming the paths as mechanisms lets a new agency reach its market through the route it can qualify for today without believing the direct door has closed forever
pros.example: placing early commercial risks through a wholesale broker while building the personal-lines volume record that supports a direct appointment application later

cons.claim: Every indirect path takes a share of the same commission and can insert someone else between the agency and the carrier relationship
cons.example: a wholesale placement where the client's servicing and renewal contact runs through the broker rather than the agency

failure_modes: waiting for direct appointments that will not come and having nothing to sell meanwhile
joining the first group that answers without comparing what its access actually adds
routing through a wholesaler risks an appointed carrier would have written, giving away both commission and the relationship
acceptance_tests: each line the charter says the agency writes has at least one identified access route with its qualification requirements, cost mechanism, ownership effect and obligation recorded, and the chosen route names the alternative rejected
revisit_triggers: a carrier opens or closes appointments in the territory
the agency's volume or loss record changes what it can qualify for
a group or wholesale relationship changes its terms

nodes.definition: If the access path is a group - aggregator, cluster, network or franchise - the membership agreement decides whether the agency is renting markets or building on them, and the terms that decide it are rarely the ones in the recruiting presentation. The classes to extract before signing are these. The fee structure and every place value leaves: initiation fee, recurring fee, percentage of commission, technology and service charges, and how contingency earned on the agency's own business is split or retained at group level. Whose name the carrier appointments are written in, because appointments held by the group mean the agency's market access ends the day membership ends. Ownership of expirations on exit, and whether the book can move to the agency's own appointments or must be sold, transferred or left behind. The exit mechanics themselves: notice period, buyout or termination fee, and how long any obligation survives departure. Production or premium minimums and what happens when they are missed. And whether the group's carriers genuinely overlap with what the chosen market needs. The decision rule is that a group is worth joining when it converts inaccessible markets into accessible ones at a cost the agency can compute, while leaving the renewals owned and the exit path written and time-bounded.

included: the full fee and value-extraction structure including how contingency is treated
whose name the appointments are written in and what that means at exit
ownership of expirations on exit, buyout and notice mechanics
production minimums and whether the group's carriers fit the chosen market
excluded: specific fee percentages, buyout formulas or minimums, which come only from the agreement in front of the agency
the general comparison of access mechanisms, which is its own work unit
book valuation, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the group's fee, appointment-name, contingency or exit terms change, or a direct appointment becomes available for the same markets

pros.claim: Extracting fees, appointment ownership and exit terms before signing turns a group decision into a computable trade instead of a leap of faith
pros.example: a group whose appointments are held in its own name is accepted only for the classes the agency cannot otherwise reach, with the rest of the book written on direct appointments

cons.claim: The comparison is asymmetric: the group knows exactly what the agency is worth to it, while the agency is evaluating markets it has never had access to
cons.example: an agency unable to judge whether the group's carrier list will actually write its niche until it has been a member for a season

failure_modes: joining for a carrier list without establishing whose name the appointments carry
missing that contingency earned on the agency's own business is retained at group level
signing an agreement with no written exit path or with an obligation that survives indefinitely
acceptance_tests: the agreement abstract records every fee and share, the appointment-name answer, the exit path with its notice and cost, the production minimums, and the specific markets the group adds that the agency cannot otherwise reach
revisit_triggers: the group changes fees, contingency treatment, carrier list or exit terms
the agency qualifies for a direct appointment that duplicates group access
a production minimum is missed or comes under pressure

nodes.definition: An appointment is not a possession; it is a relationship the carrier reviews. Carriers expect an agency to produce premium and to produce it profitably, and they measure both - written and in-force premium, growth, retention, hit ratio on submissions, and loss ratio on the business placed - then act on what they see. The actions to plan for are a production requirement written into the agreement, a warning and improvement period, restriction of the appointment to certain lines or classes, placement into run-off where renewals continue but new business stops, and outright termination on the notice the contract specifies. The practical consequence for a small agency is that appointments cost something to hold even when idle: spread across too many markets, the agency feeds none of them well, learns none of their products or systems properly, and loses the ones it most needed. The management discipline is therefore to hold the smallest set of markets that honestly covers the chosen focus, direct enough volume to each to matter, watch the loss-ratio signal the way the carrier watches it, keep a written concentration limit so no single market holds a share of the book the agency could not rehouse, and open the conversation with the underwriter or marketing representative before the carrier opens it with the agency.

included: the metrics carriers judge an appointment by: volume, growth, retention, hit ratio and loss ratio
the escalation path from warning through restriction and run-off to termination
the cost of holding appointments the agency cannot feed or learn
the written concentration limit and proactive contact with the carrier's representative
excluded: remarketing an individual client at renewal and the retention practices around it, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns
specific volume thresholds or loss-ratio targets, which come from each carrier's own agreement and communications

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier's performance feedback, production requirement or appetite in the territory changes

pros.claim: Concentrating volume in a few well-fed markets earns better underwriter attention, faster answers and a more defensible position when a bad loss year arrives
pros.example: an underwriter who knows the agency's submissions works a marginal risk instead of declining it on sight

cons.claim: Concentration is itself a risk, because if the primary market withdraws from the territory or restricts the class, a large share of the book needs a new home at once
cons.example: a carrier pulling back from a coastal county where much of the agency's homeowners book sits

failure_modes: accepting every appointment offered and feeding none of them
discovering a production shortfall from the termination notice rather than from the agency's own tracking
letting one carrier hold a share of the book the agency could not rehouse quickly
acceptance_tests: for each appointed carrier the agency tracks its own placed volume, retention and loss-ratio signal against the agreement's expectations, and no single carrier holds a share of the book above the written concentration limit
revisit_triggers: a carrier issues a production warning, restriction or run-off notice
a large claim materially moves loss ratio with a core carrier
a carrier withdraws from a class or territory the agency depends on

nodes.definition: Work out, in the agency's own numbers, how long it must fund itself before commission covers cost, because the structural feature of property and casualty is that revenue arrives thin and late while cost arrives early and monthly. The mechanism has two sides. Cost classes: licensing and entity fees, errors-and-omissions premium, an agency management system, a comparative rater and carrier system access, group or franchise fees where applicable, any required bond, marketing and lead spend, office and communications, and the operator's own living cost. Revenue mechanism: a new policy pays commission on a single premium, and it is the renewal a year later that begins compounding, so the first year is paid for by new business alone and cancellations reverse part of even that. The model is built only from the agency's own commission schedules and measured results - expected policies bound per month, the mix of lines and their rates, the lag from bound to statement, and an assumed reversal rate - run against the monthly cost base until the crossing point appears. Contingency is excluded from it entirely. The output is a runway expressed in months with its assumptions named and a checkpoint schedule at which each assumption is re-measured against actual statements.

included: the one-time and recurring cost classes a new property and casualty agency carries
the timing mechanism by which commission lags cost and renewals compound only later
building the model from the agency's own schedules, measured bind rates and reversal experience
runway expressed in months with named assumptions and re-measurement checkpoints
excluded: any specific amount, industry-average cost or benchmark revenue-per-account figure
financing, entity and tax structuring decisions, which belong to the agency's accountant and lender
book valuation and exit proceeds, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured bind volume, commission timing, reversal experience or the monthly cost base changes

pros.claim: A runway model with named assumptions turns an unanswerable question into a small number of measurable quantities the agency can watch monthly
pros.example: seeing that the crossing point moves more with the monthly bind count than with any single cost line, and directing effort there

cons.claim: Every input is an estimate until a full statement cycle exists, so early versions of the model are wrong in ways the agency cannot yet detect
cons.example: a first model built before any commercial audit adjustment or flat cancel had ever appeared on a statement

failure_modes: counting written business as income before statements clear and reversals settle
including contingency income in the runway model
committing to fixed costs sized for a book that does not exist yet
acceptance_tests: the model states each cost class, the revenue timing and reversal assumptions, excludes contingency, produces a runway in months, and has been re-measured against actual statements at the most recent checkpoint
revisit_triggers: actual bound volume, line mix or reversal rate diverges from the model
a fixed cost is added or a group fee changes
the runway falls below the reserve threshold the agency has written down

nodes.definition: Decide which market the agency is actually built for, because personal lines and small commercial are different businesses that happen to share one license. Personal lines - auto, homeowners, renters, condominium, landlord and umbrella - means many small accounts, comparatively standardized products, faster sales cycles, heavy price shopping, and a service load driven by vehicle changes, address changes, mortgagee changes and post-storm questions. Small commercial - business owners policies, general liability, commercial auto, workers compensation and small property - means fewer and larger accounts, longer sales cycles anchored to renewal dates, far more underwriting judgment, deeper relationships, certificates and payroll or receipts audits as recurring work, and materially higher stakes when the coverage is wrong. The choice is made against four things the agency can genuinely assess: which carriers it can access for that market through the paths open to it, whether a referral ecosystem for it exists in this territory, whether the agency has or can build the technical competence the market demands, and whether its service capacity matches the account's touch rate. A mixed book is legitimate and common, but it has to be chosen and staffed rather than accumulated, and the decision is written with the segment the agency is explicitly not chasing this year.

included: the structural differences between personal lines and small commercial as businesses
the four assessment criteria of accessible carriers, referral ecosystem, technical competence and service capacity
a deliberate mix with a stated segment not being chased this year
the decision written and dated with a re-test point
excluded: coverage design and limit selection within either segment, which the quoting knowledge base owns
large or hazardous commercial risks, which the charter refers to a specialist
life, health and employee-benefits lines, which require other licenses

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: carrier access, measured segment economics or the referral ecosystem for the chosen segment changes

pros.claim: Choosing the market before the carriers, the systems and the marketing stops the agency from being staffed for one business while selling another
pros.example: an agency choosing small commercial builds toward carriers with real small-business appetite and a referral relationship with an accountant rather than buying personal auto leads

cons.claim: A narrow focus forgoes revenue the agency could have written and feels indefensible during a slow month
cons.example: declining to chase personal auto shoppers while the commercial pipeline is still filling

failure_modes: letting the focus be decided by whichever leads happen to be cheapest to buy
choosing commercial without the technical competence its coverage decisions require
running a mixed book with no staffing plan so both segments receive partial attention
acceptance_tests: the focus decision names the primary segment, the secondary if any, and the segment not being chased, states the evidence behind all four criteria, and carries a date and a re-test point
revisit_triggers: carrier access for the chosen segment changes materially
measured service load or close time diverges from what the choice assumed
the referral ecosystem for the chosen segment changes

nodes.definition: Compare the lines the agency could write on the three quantities that decide whether they are worth writing: what each account yields, what it costs in service time, and what it exposes the agency to when something goes wrong. Yield is a mechanism rather than a number - premium size multiplied by the schedule's commission rate for that line, adjusted for how much of it renews and at what rate. Service load is the count of touches a policy generates in a year: personal auto produces vehicle and driver changes and frequent small claims contact; homeowners produces mortgagee changes, inspection and roof issues, and a wave of questions after every storm; commercial lines produce certificates of insurance, mid-term additions, payroll and receipts audits, and renewal underwriting information requests. Exposure is the errors-and-omissions severity if the coverage turns out to be wrong, which is modest on a renters policy and severe on a contractor's liability or a workers compensation classification. The agency measures its own touch counts rather than importing anyone else's, and what the comparison produces is not which line pays best but which line pays best per hour of the agency's real capacity at an exposure it can carry - which is what actually caps how many accounts it can hold.

included: yield as a per-line mechanism of premium, rate and renewal behaviour
service load measured as annual touches per account by line from the agency's own records
errors-and-omissions severity as the third axis of the comparison
an account capacity derived from the measurement and written down
excluded: any published average premium, commission rate, revenue-per-account or hours-per-policy figure
retention improvement and remarketing decisions, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns
coverage content and limit choice within a line

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured per-line touch counts, commission terms for a line, or the agency's real capacity changes

pros.claim: Measuring touches per account exposes the accounts that quietly lose money and caps growth before service quality collapses
pros.example: a low-premium personal auto segment generating more service contacts per year than a commercial package worth several times as much

cons.claim: Honest touch measurement takes months, and any early comparison rests on a sample too small to trust
cons.example: a first-quarter estimate skewed by one storm season that inflated homeowners service contacts

failure_modes: comparing lines on commission rate alone and taking on a service load the agency cannot carry
ignoring errors-and-omissions severity differences when deciding what to chase
growing account count past capacity and discovering the cost later as missed endorsements
acceptance_tests: each line the agency writes has its yield mechanism, measured annual touch count and exposure severity class recorded from the agency's own data, and a stated account capacity derived from them
revisit_triggers: measured touch counts move outside the recorded band
a carrier changes commission or service arrangements for a line
staffing, systems or process change the agency's real capacity

nodes.definition: Before marketing to a niche, prove the agency can actually place it. A niche in property and casualty is a class of risk the agency intends to become the obvious choice for - a trade such as landscapers or auto repair shops, a property type such as older homes in one neighbourhood, a community the agency genuinely belongs to, or a situation such as first-time homebuyers arriving through a lender relationship - and its value is that repeated exposure builds real underwriting knowledge, faster quoting and referral gravity. What makes niche selection a discipline rather than a slogan is the failure mode of choosing a class none of the agency's markets want. Carrier appetite is specific and it moves: it lives in eligibility guides, class codes, construction and protection-class rules, prior-loss and experience requirements, and it is withdrawn when a book underperforms or a catastrophe changes the view of a territory. So the work is to build an appetite map from each carrier's own guides and from actual submission outcomes, confirm a primary and a backup home for the niche's typical risk, identify the variants that will need a wholesale or surplus-lines route, and only then commit marketing to it. The map is dated and maintained, because appetite that existed at launch is a claim about the past.

included: defining a niche as a repeatable class the agency intends to own
building an appetite map from carrier eligibility guides and real submission outcomes
requiring a primary and a backup market plus a route for the hard variants before marketing
maintaining and dating the map as appetite moves
excluded: individual risk selection and underwriting judgment on a specific submission, which the quoting knowledge base owns
the referral relationships that feed the niche, which are their own work unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier's eligibility guide, class appetite, or the agency's submission outcomes in the niche change

pros.claim: Testing appetite before marketing prevents the most expensive niche failure, which is a pipeline of risks the agency has nowhere to place
