pros.example: discovering during appetite mapping that only one market will write the roofing contractors a referral partner would have sent, and choosing a different trade

cons.claim: Appetite mapping is perishable work that must be redone as carriers restrict classes, so the map is never finished
cons.example: a market that welcomed a class in spring closing it after a poor loss year, invalidating part of the map

failure_modes: marketing to a niche before confirming any market will write it
relying on a single carrier's appetite to carry the whole niche
treating a marketing representative's verbal encouragement as an appetite commitment
acceptance_tests: the niche has a written appetite map naming a primary and a backup market for its typical risk, the known ineligible variants and their route, each entry sourced to a carrier guide or a real submission outcome and dated
revisit_triggers: a carrier restricts, withdraws or reprices the niche class
submissions in the niche begin being declined at an unusual rate
a catastrophe or regulatory change alters appetite across the territory

nodes.definition: Build the set of channels that bring the chosen market to the agency, and put each one through the conduct rules before it starts rather than after. The channel classes in property and casualty are relationship referrals from mortgage lenders, real-estate agents, auto dealers, accountants, attorneys and contractors; association and community membership where the agency genuinely participates; existing clients and their households; direct response through search, local content and reviews; purchased leads and comparison-shopping platforms; and outbound contact into a defined list. The conduct rules governing them are not decorative. Compensating a referral source may implicate the state's anti-rebating and inducement rules, and where the referral comes from a real-estate settlement-service provider a separate federal regime governs what may be paid for a referral at all - both are obligation classes to verify with counsel and the state department before any money or gift changes hands. Telephone and text outreach carries do-not-call and consent obligations; purchased leads raise the question of whether the consumer knowingly consented to be contacted about insurance; and prospect information carries privacy and safeguarding duties from the first record onward. Each channel is therefore documented with its consent basis, its cost mechanism measured in the agency's own numbers, and its measured conversion into bound accounts that stay.

included: the channel classes that produce property and casualty accounts and how each is opened
the conduct obligation classes of rebating and inducement, settlement-service referral limits, do-not-call and consent, and prospect-data privacy
documenting each channel's consent basis and measured cost per bound account
retiring channels that cannot be run cleanly
excluded: the legality of any particular referral arrangement, fee or gift, which is verified with counsel and the state department in the operating jurisdiction
the sales conversation and needs analysis with a prospect, which the quoting knowledge base owns
client-referral cultivation from an existing book, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a channel's consent basis, compensation arrangement or measured cost per bound account changes

pros.claim: Clearing a channel's consent and compensation basis before it starts keeps a productive source from becoming a complaint or an enforcement matter later
pros.example: structuring a lender relationship as genuine co-marketing at fair value rather than a per-referral payment, after checking the rules that apply

cons.claim: The cleanest channels are the slowest to build, so an agency under cash pressure faces constant temptation from faster and murkier sources
cons.example: a purchased lead source with strong volume whose consumers plainly did not expect an insurance call

failure_modes: paying for referrals without checking rebating, inducement and settlement-service rules first
contacting purchased leads with no verifiable consent basis
measuring channels on lead volume rather than on bound accounts that stay
acceptance_tests: every active channel has a recorded consent basis, a compensation arrangement checked against the rebating, inducement and settlement-service obligation classes, and a measured cost per bound account from the agency's own data
revisit_triggers: a channel's consent basis, compensation structure or vendor changes
a regulator, carrier or consumer raises a marketing or contact concern
a channel's measured cost per bound account drifts outside its band

nodes.definition: Set the standard for how the agency opens and conducts every consumer conversation, and hold it as a condition of doing business rather than a preference. The opening is disclosure-first: the producer's name, the agency, that this is a licensed insurance agency, whether it represents one carrier or several, and the purpose of the contact, all stated before any information is collected. Three prohibitions follow. No fear-selling: catastrophe, liability and lawsuit exposure are described factually, from the policy's own terms and the client's actual situation, never dramatized to force a decision. No savings promise: premium and eligibility are determined by carriers through their own rating and underwriting, so the agency offers to shop and to explain and never states or implies that a consumer will pay less, that a quote will hold, or that coverage exists before the carrier confirms it. No manufactured urgency: real deadlines such as a closing date, a renewal date or a cancellation notice are stated plainly, and nothing else is presented as one. Vulnerable-consumer care belongs to the same standard: with older clients, consumers under disaster stress, and those with limited English or literacy, the agency slows down, provides a written summary, welcomes a family member or trusted adviser into the conversation, and stops if the consumer does not appear to understand what is being decided.

included: the disclosure-first opening and everything it must state
the prohibitions on fear-selling, savings promises and manufactured urgency
vulnerable-consumer care as a required practice with concrete accommodations
the standard applied identically across every channel, script and asset
excluded: the needs-analysis conversation and the coverage recommendation itself, which the quoting knowledge base owns
claims-time communication, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns
state-specific advertising filing, title and disclosure specifics, which are verified in the operating jurisdiction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint, a regulatory change or a new channel changes what the contact standard must cover

pros.claim: A single disclosed opening makes every later step defensible and is the cheapest protection against the complaint class that begins with not knowing who was calling
pros.example: an inbound comparison-platform lead answered by naming the agency, its licensed status and the several carriers it represents before a single rating question is asked

cons.claim: Full disclosure up front costs some conversations that a vaguer opening would have kept alive long enough to build interest
cons.example: a consumer ending the call once told immediately that this is an insurance agency and not the lender they were expecting

failure_modes: using a script that hides or softens the insurance purpose to improve response rates
answering a savings question with a promise rather than an explanation of how carriers set premium
pushing a disaster-stressed or confused consumer to decide within the same conversation
acceptance_tests: every script, voicemail, mailer and landing page in use opens with identification and purpose, contains no savings promise or dramatized risk language, and the vulnerable-consumer accommodations are written into the process rather than left to judgment
revisit_triggers: a complaint, carrier concern or regulator inquiry touches how contact was made
a new channel, vendor or script is introduced
advertising or contact rules change in an operating state

nodes.definition: Name the conflict the agency lives inside and decide in advance how it will be resolved, because it recurs on almost every placement. The agency is paid by the carrier it places business with, rates differ by carrier and line, contingency rewards volume and low loss ratio with particular carriers, and group or wholesale arrangements change what the agency keeps - so there will be cases where the carrier that pays the agency best is not the carrier that serves the client best. The resolution is procedural rather than aspirational: placement follows a documented comparison of coverage, the carrier's ability to pay and service a claim, financial strength, and price, with the reason for the carrier chosen recorded in the file at the time; and if the choice would be different absent compensation, the client's carrier wins and that reasoning is written down. Around this sits disclosure practice. The agency states plainly whether it represents one carrier or several, answers honestly and without deflection when a client asks how it is paid, and treats any charge to the client beyond commission - a broker or service fee - as a regulated question whose legality, disclosure and written-consent requirements differ by state and must be verified before it is ever charged. An agency that cannot explain its compensation in one plain sentence has a problem to fix, not a disclosure to avoid.

included: the structural conflict between commission, contingency, split arrangements and client fit
the procedural resolution of a documented comparison with the reason for the carrier chosen recorded
honest answers about who the agency represents and how it is paid
broker and service fees as a regulated class to verify before charging
excluded: specific commission or fee amounts, and whether a particular fee is lawful in a given state, which is verified with the department and counsel
the coverage comparison itself, which the quoting knowledge base owns
contingency formula mechanics, which are their own work unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a compensation arrangement, a fee practice, or a challenge to a placement rationale changes the picture

pros.claim: A written placement rationale makes the conflict visible and answerable, and it is the same record that defends the placement years later
pros.example: a file showing a lower-commission carrier chosen for its claims handling on a coastal home, with the reason recorded at the time rather than reconstructed afterwards

cons.claim: Documenting a rationale on every placement is friction on the busiest part of the workflow and is the first discipline to slip under volume
cons.example: a high-volume week where placement reasons are recorded thinly and the file loses its explanation

failure_modes: placing business to reach a contingency threshold and calling it a judgment call
deflecting a direct question about how the agency is paid
charging a client fee without verifying its legality, disclosure and consent requirements in that state
acceptance_tests: placement files in the period carry a recorded reason for the carrier chosen, the agency can state its representation and compensation in one plain sentence, and any client-charged fee has a documented legality and consent basis for that state
revisit_triggers: compensation terms change through a carrier, group or wholesale arrangement
a client or regulator questions a placement or a fee
the agency begins charging a fee or changes its fee practice

nodes.definition: Hold one gate between building the agency and selling insurance, and pass every item before the first consumer conversation. The pass conditions are the outputs of everything upstream: the individual license active with the property and casualty lines of authority; the business-entity license active with its designated responsible producer where the state requires one; an access route in force for every line the charter says the agency writes, with appointments confirmed by carrier and state; errors-and-omissions coverage bound at or above every agreement's required limit with its retroactive date recorded; each agency or group agreement abstracted for ownership of expirations, binding authority, commission mechanism and termination; the obligation calendar populated with owners and lead times; an agency management system and a documentation template in place so the first file is as defensible as the hundredth; the disclosure-first contact standard written into every script and asset in use; the refusal and referral list with named homes; and a runway model with a checkpoint date. An item that cannot pass is never waived - it either blocks the class of business it governs or is closed before selling begins, and the failed condition is named in writing. The gate is re-run whenever a state, carrier, group, line or owner changes, because each of those quietly invalidates one of its conditions.

included: the complete pass-condition set spanning licensing, authority, coverage, contracts, calendar, systems, conduct and runway
the rule that a failed condition blocks the class of business it governs rather than being waived
re-running the gate on any change of state, carrier, group, line or ownership
excluded: the per-account file standard and the quote-to-bind checklist, which the quoting and binding knowledge base owns
renewal and retention readiness, which the renewals and book value knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any upstream licensing, appointment, coverage, contract or conduct artifact changes state

pros.claim: One gate turns a scattered set of prerequisites into a single pass or fail that cannot be quietly skipped under revenue pressure
pros.example: a pending nonresident license blocking quoting in that state while the agency keeps writing everywhere it is already authorized

cons.claim: A strict gate delays the first revenue and feels indefensible when a real prospect is waiting behind a paperwork item
cons.example: turning away a referred account because the carrier appointment for its line has not yet been confirmed in writing

failure_modes: waiving a condition for one account only
passing the gate once and never re-running it after adding a state, a carrier or a line
treating documentation and system readiness as optional because the first files are few
acceptance_tests: every pass condition is evidenced with its artifact and date, no condition is waived, and each failed condition is recorded with the class of business it currently blocks
revisit_triggers: a state, carrier, group, line of business or ownership change occurs
any upstream artifact expires or is superseded
an errors-and-omissions, complaint or audit event calls a condition into question

edges.why_related: the lines the charter says the agency will write decide which lines of authority the license must carry
an entity license is built around licensed people and normally requires a designated responsible producer who already holds an active individual license
nonresident licenses are commonly issued on the strength of an active resident license through reciprocity rather than by re-examination
what the agency intends to sell and refuse determines which affiliation models can actually deliver it
the charter's lines and refusals bound the segments the focus decision is allowed to choose between
the model chosen determines which agreements exist and therefore which ownership and covenant clauses must be abstracted
whether the agency is captive, independent or inside a group changes who requires errors-and-omissions coverage, at what limit, and whose policy responds
carrier agreements and appointments are filed to the licensed entity, so the entity credential must exist before contracting
evidence of errors-and-omissions coverage at the carrier's required limit is a standard item in the contracting packet
the affiliation model decides which access mechanisms are available to the agency at all
which markets have to be opened is decided by the segment the agency has chosen to serve
a group membership agreement is only read in detail once a group has been selected as one of the access paths
binding authority is a grant inside the agency agreement and only exists once the appointment does
the commission schedule is part of the same agency agreement the appointment attaches to
contingency is computed on the same placed premium base that commission is paid on and is only interpretable against it
the production and performance expectations to be managed are set in the agreement that created the appointment
the lines whose yield, service load and exposure must be compared are the ones the chosen focus puts in play
the runway model needs per-line yield and measured capacity to convert bound accounts into expected revenue
a niche is chosen inside the segment the focus decision has already fixed
the contact standard opens by stating licensed status, which presupposes that the license actually exists
every appointment adds maintenance obligations the calendar has to carry with owners and lead times
the gate checks that every recurring obligation has an owner, a lead time and current evidence before selling begins
acting outside a written binding grant is the exposure the errors-and-omissions program is least able to defend, so the coverage constrains how the authority may be used
an access path is only acceptable if the ownership and exit terms it carries leave the renewals with the agency
marketing may only be aimed at states where the producer and a carrier both hold authority for the risk
a channel is only usable if its contacts can be opened with full identification, a verifiable consent basis and no savings promise
a formula rewarding volume and low loss ratio with a particular carrier pulls placements toward that carrier while the client's interest may point elsewhere
edges.resolution_rule: placement follows the documented comparison of coverage, claims handling, financial strength and price with the reason recorded in the file; if the carrier choice would change absent compensation, the client's carrier is chosen and the reason written down, and contingency is never carried as budgeted revenue

edges.why_related: a carrier's production expectation pushes business toward it while the appetite map may say the risk belongs somewhere else
edges.resolution_rule: never place a risk to feed a quota: place to appetite and client fit, and if the agency cannot honestly feed an appointment, reduce the number of appointments or accept the carrier's restriction rather than misplacing risks

edges.why_related: group membership buys market access immediately but can condition or encumber ownership of the expirations written through it
edges.resolution_rule: join only when expirations remain owned by the agency and the exit path is written, costed and time-bounded; where appointments are held in the group's name, treat that access as rented and cap the share of the book placed through it

edges.why_related: the paths that open markets fastest take a share of commission or charge fees, while waiting for direct appointments preserves economics but extends the period with nothing to sell
edges.resolution_rule: choose the path that keeps the agency solvent through the ramp while leaving the renewals owned, and re-evaluate at the runway model's checkpoints as the volume record makes direct appointments reachable

edges.why_related: the segment with better per-account economics usually has the longer sales cycle and slower cash, while the faster-paying segment demands volume the agency may not be able to service
edges.resolution_rule: size the mix to the runway: carry enough of the faster-cycling segment to cover the monthly cost base while the longer-cycle pipeline builds, and re-test the mix at each checkpoint against measured close times

edges.why_related: when commission is earned, when it settles and when it reverses is what actually creates or consumes runway, more than any single cost line
sustained volume, retention and loss-ratio performance is the mechanism that keeps an appointment in force or causes it to be restricted or terminated
service load carried beyond real capacity is the mechanism that produces missed endorsements and unanswered coverage requests, which is where errors-and-omissions claims come from
the ownership, termination and covenant clauses are abstracted before the agreement is signed and the appointment filed, because none of them can be renegotiated afterwards
channels are built after the segment is chosen, because who the agency serves determines which referral ecosystems exist for it
a niche with no primary or backup home on the current shelf sends the agency back to open a wholesale, surplus-lines or additional market
a condition that fails at the gate is returned to the obligation calendar with an owner and a lead time until it can pass

both are recurring maintenance disciplines whose failure mode is the silent loss of something already earned - a license in one case, an appointment in the other - so they are reviewed on the same rhythm

conflict_axes.name: captive_support_vs_independent_ownership
conflict_axes.description: Training, systems, brand, carrier access and early subsidy come from the models that most restrict product choice and most often condition the customer relationship, while ownership of the renewals and freedom of placement come with the full cost of running a business alone.
poles: take the support and accept the restrictions
take ownership and carry the whole cost
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide on the four durable axes - who owns the expirations, what leaving costs, what carrier access the model really delivers for the chosen market, and what the bundled support is worth priced against buying it directly - and weight any first-year subsidy last

conflict_axes.name: market_access_now_vs_ownership_and_economics_later
conflict_axes.description: Group, franchise and wholesale paths put markets in the agency's hands immediately at the price of fees, commission share and sometimes appointments held in someone else's name, while holding out for direct appointments preserves economics and ownership but leaves the agency with little to sell during the ramp.
poles: buy access now and pay for it
wait for direct appointments and preserve economics
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sequence the paths: use the fastest access the agency qualifies for on the classes it cannot otherwise place, keep the expirations owned, and convert to direct appointments as the volume and loss record makes them reachable

conflict_axes.name: carrier_breadth_vs_volume_concentration
conflict_axes.description: More appointments cover more risks and reduce dependence on any one market, but every appointment must be fed with volume and learned properly, and a thin book spread across many carriers satisfies none of them while a concentrated book is exposed if its main market withdraws.
poles: carry more markets for coverage
concentrate volume in fewer markets for standing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the smallest set of markets that honestly covers the chosen focus with a primary and a backup per class, and write down a concentration limit above which the agency will not let one carrier hold the book

conflict_axes.name: compensation_pull_vs_client_fit
conflict_axes.description: Commission rates differ by carrier and line, contingency rewards volume and low loss ratio with particular carriers, and group or wholesale splits change what the agency keeps, so there will be placements where the best-paying market is not the best-serving one.
poles: place where the agency earns most
place where the client is served best
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: resolve procedurally rather than aspirationally: compare coverage, claims handling, financial strength and price, record the reason for the carrier chosen, and if the choice would differ absent compensation, choose the client's carrier and write down why

conflict_axes.name: personal_lines_volume_vs_commercial_depth
conflict_axes.description: Personal lines offers many small, faster-closing, price-shopped accounts with a steady service load, while small commercial offers fewer, larger, slower-closing accounts with deeper relationships, more underwriting judgment and materially higher stakes when coverage is wrong.
poles: build on personal-lines volume
build on small-commercial depth
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose against accessible carriers, referral ecosystem, technical competence and service capacity, staff for the choice, and name the segment the agency is explicitly not chasing this year rather than drifting between them

conflict_axes.name: growth_pace_vs_service_capacity
conflict_axes.description: Every account added is revenue now and service obligation for years, and the point where account count passes real capacity is invisible until it shows up as missed endorsements, unanswered coverage requests and the errors-and-omissions claims that follow.
poles: take every account the pipeline produces
cap growth at measured service capacity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: derive a written account capacity from measured touch counts per line and hold new business at that ceiling until staffing, systems or process change the measurement

conflict_axes.name: binding_speed_vs_authority_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Binding on the spot wins accounts and delights clients, while every referral to an underwriter costs time the competitor may not spend - but a placement made outside the written grant can leave the client uncovered and the gap with the agency.
poles: bind fast to win the account
stay strictly inside the written grant
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make the grant visible at the point of sale so the fast yes is always a legitimate one, and treat anything outside it as a documented referral with the client told plainly that coverage is not in force until the carrier confirms

conflict_axes.name: price_message_vs_coverage_honesty
conflict_axes.description: Price is what the market responds to and what every competitor advertises, but premium and eligibility are carrier-determined and a message built on promised savings sets up a consumer to be under-covered and the agency to be blamed.
poles: lead with price to get the conversation
lead with coverage and refuse savings promises
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: offer to shop and to explain how carriers set premium, never state or imply savings or that a quote will hold, and let the comparison of what is actually covered carry the conversation

conflict_axes.name: footprint_expansion_vs_maintenance_load
conflict_axes.description: Adding states captures clients who move, own property elsewhere or operate across a line, but every added state carries its own license, renewal, education interaction, appointment filings and possibly surplus-lines duties for volume that may never justify them.
poles: license broadly to keep every client
keep a narrow footprint and refer the rest
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: add a state when a recurring, evidenced flow of business exists there rather than for a single account, and use recorded referrals to licensed producers for everything outside the footprint

conflict_axes.name: niche_depth_vs_market_availability
conflict_axes.description: Specializing in one class builds underwriting knowledge, referral gravity and faster quoting, but carrier appetite for that class can be restricted or withdrawn after a bad loss year or a catastrophe, leaving a marketing engine pointed at risks the agency can no longer place.
poles: go deep in one class
stay broad enough to survive an appetite withdrawal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require a primary and a backup market plus a wholesale path for the hard variants before marketing to a niche, and keep the appetite map dated and maintained rather than treated as settled

edge_cases.description: Mid-quote the agency discovers the property or the garaging address sits in a state where neither the producer nor the carrier holds authority
edge_cases.trigger: a risk's true location differs from the client's mailing address or from where the conversation started
edge_cases.mitigation: stop the quote, tell the client plainly that the agency is not authorized for that location, refer to a producer licensed there and record the referral, and decide separately and later whether the flow justifies adding the state

edge_cases.description: A carrier terminates or restricts an appointment for production or loss-ratio reasons and a share of the book has to find a new home
edge_cases.trigger: a termination, restriction or run-off notice arrives from a market the agency depends on
edge_cases.mitigation: read the notice for run-off versus immediate effect and for what happens to renewals and commission, open or activate the backup market for the affected classes before touching clients, and hand the client-facing remarketing sequence to the renewals process rather than improvising it

edge_cases.description: The agency changes errors-and-omissions carriers and the new policy is issued with a fresh retroactive date, stranding every placement made before it
edge_cases.trigger: a coverage change, lapse or gap in the claims-made program
edge_cases.mitigation: treat retroactive-date continuity and prior-acts coverage as a non-negotiable condition of any change, obtain tail coverage where continuity cannot be preserved, and never allow a gap between policies

edge_cases.description: The group holds the carrier appointments in its own name, so leaving would end the agency's access to the very markets its book is written in
edge_cases.trigger: a membership agreement where appointments and carrier relationships sit at group level
edge_cases.mitigation: establish the appointment-name answer before signing, cap the share of the book placed through group-held appointments, and build at least one directly appointed market for the core classes so an exit is survivable

edge_cases.description: A referral partner such as a lender or real-estate agent asks for a per-referral payment or a gift in exchange for sending business
edge_cases.trigger: a compensation request from a referral source, particularly one tied to a real-estate settlement
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as a regulated question before any money or gift moves - the state's rebating and inducement rules and, for settlement-service referrals, a separate federal regime both apply - and verify with counsel and the department, restructuring as genuine co-marketing at fair value or declining

edge_cases.description: A client needs coverage bound before a closing or renewal deadline on a risk that falls outside the delegated binding grant, or during a catastrophe moratorium
edge_cases.trigger: a deadline collides with a prohibited class, an out-of-grant condition or a suspension event
edge_cases.mitigation: do not bind outside the grant; submit the referral immediately with the deadline stated, tell the client in writing that coverage is not in force until the carrier confirms, and offer the wholesale or surplus-lines path rather than an assurance the agency cannot back

edge_cases.description: A carrier withdraws appetite for the exact class the agency built its niche marketing around
edge_cases.trigger: an eligibility guide change, class restriction or territory withdrawal after a poor loss year or a catastrophe
edge_cases.mitigation: pause marketing into the class, re-run the appetite map for a primary and a backup home including wholesale routes, and if none exists, change the niche rather than continuing to generate risks with nowhere to go

edge_cases.description: A consumer under disaster stress, an older client, or someone with limited English or literacy is being asked to decide quickly about coverage
edge_cases.trigger: a vulnerable-consumer situation, often after a storm, fire or a cancellation notice
edge_cases.mitigation: slow the conversation, provide a written summary of what is and is not covered, invite a family member or trusted adviser to join, avoid any urgency that is not a real deadline, and stop if the consumer does not appear to understand what is being decided

edge_cases.description: Commission statements stop reconciling: a month of strong new business nets far less than expected after flat cancels, downward endorsements and a commercial audit
edge_cases.trigger: return commission and adjustments landing on a later statement cycle
edge_cases.mitigation: reconcile each statement against the recorded rate, base and settlement mechanism per carrier, carry a reversal assumption in the runway model, and never treat written-premium commission as cash before the statement clears

edge_cases.description: Contingency income that was mentally spent arrives far below expectation or not at all after one severe claim moves loss ratio
edge_cases.trigger: a measurement period closing on a small book that absorbed a large loss
edge_cases.mitigation: keep contingency out of the committed cost budget entirely, model it only as an uncertain bonus from the carrier's own schedule, and re-examine whether any placement pattern was quietly bent toward a threshold

edge_cases.description: The designated responsible producer leaves, or the individual license behind the entity license lapses, while appointments and in-force business continue
edge_cases.trigger: a personnel change or a missed renewal on the individual credential the entity depends on
edge_cases.mitigation: stop soliciting, notify the department and affected carriers, name a qualified replacement responsible producer, confirm the status of pending business and any reinstatement path, and re-run the readiness gate before resuming

edge_cases.description: A prospect asks the agency to promise a lower premium than their current policy before any information has been gathered
edge_cases.trigger: a price-led inquiry, often from a comparison platform or a mailer response
edge_cases.mitigation: explain that premium and eligibility are set by carriers through their own rating and underwriting, offer to shop and to compare what is actually covered, and give no savings promise, no guarantee that a quote will hold, and no assurance of coverage before the carrier confirms it

workflow.action: Write the agency scope and refusal charter
workflow.description: State the lines the agency writes, the classes it refuses, where each refusal goes, and the standing no-advice and no-guarantee language
workflow.artifact: agency charter with refusal list and named referral homes
workflow.gate: the lines written, at least three refusal classes each with a named referral home, and the standing carrier-determined-premium sentence are written and match every planned marketing asset

workflow.action: Complete the resident producer licensing path
workflow.description: Identify the state's current requirement classes in order, complete each, and file the artifact it produces
workflow.artifact: active individual license record with property and casualty lines of authority and a filed evidence set
workflow.gate: the license shows the property and casualty lines of authority active with its number and expiration, and every requirement class has a matching artifact

workflow.action: License the agency entity and name the responsible producer
workflow.description: Obtain the business-entity license where required, register and clear the trade name, and record the supervision boundary over unlicensed staff
workflow.artifact: entity license record with responsible producer, trade-name registration and supervision note
workflow.gate: the entity license is active, the responsible producer on file is the person performing the role, and the advertising name matches the licensed or registered name

workflow.action: Decide the affiliation model on the four durable axes
workflow.description: Compare captive, independent, franchise and employed-producer operation on relationship ownership, exit cost, real carrier access and the priced value of bundled support
workflow.artifact: written model decision with the contract language behind each axis and the rejected alternative
workflow.gate: each of the four axes is answered from actual contract language and at least one rejected alternative is recorded with its reason

workflow.action: Select the market focus and test it against capacity
workflow.description: Choose the primary segment across personal and small-commercial lines against accessible carriers, referral ecosystem, technical competence and service capacity
workflow.artifact: dated market focus decision naming the primary segment and the segment not being chased
workflow.gate: the decision states the evidence behind all four criteria, names what is not being chased this year, and carries a re-test date

workflow.action: Bind the errors-and-omissions program before contracting
workflow.description: Place coverage with the retroactive date, limit and deductible recorded, disclosing the classes the agency intends to write
workflow.artifact: errors-and-omissions policy record with retroactive date and limit, and the disclosure made on the application
workflow.gate: coverage is in force at or above every intended agency agreement's required limit, with the retroactive date recorded and the disclosed classes matching the charter

workflow.action: Open carrier access through the path the agency can qualify for
workflow.description: Evaluate direct appointment, group membership, franchise, wholesale and surplus-lines routes per line on qualification, cost, ownership effect and obligation created
workflow.artifact: access plan naming a route for every line in the charter with its four evaluation answers
workflow.gate: each line the charter says the agency writes has at least one identified route with its qualification requirements, cost mechanism, ownership effect and obligation recorded

workflow.action: Abstract every agreement before signing it
workflow.description: Extract ownership of expirations, termination with and without cause, run-off, covenants, assignment and the commission and binding references from each carrier or group agreement
workflow.gate: for every agreement in front of the agency, the abstract answers who owns expirations, what happens on each termination type, the covenant terms and duration, and whether the book may be assigned

workflow.action: Complete appointments and build the authority register
workflow.description: Submit contracting packets, confirm appointment status per carrier and state, and record binding grants, production expectations and termination provisions
workflow.artifact: authority register covering every carrier and state with dates, binding grant and termination terms
workflow.gate: every carrier and state the agency will write shows an in-force appointment or a verified filing-window rule, with the binding grant and the production expectation recorded alongside it

workflow.action: Model the runway from the agency's own numbers
workflow.description: Assemble cost classes and the commission timing, mix and reversal assumptions into months of runway with checkpoints
workflow.artifact: runway model with named assumptions and a checkpoint schedule
workflow.gate: the model states each cost class, the revenue timing and reversal assumptions, excludes contingency entirely, and produces a runway in months with a first checkpoint date

workflow.action: Build the referral architecture and the contact standard
workflow.description: Open the channels for the chosen segment and clear each one's consent basis and compensation arrangement before it starts
workflow.artifact: channel register with consent basis, compensation arrangement and measurement plan per channel
workflow.gate: every active channel has a recorded consent basis, a compensation arrangement checked against the rebating, inducement and settlement-service obligation classes, and a defined measure of cost per bound account

workflow.action: Pass the readiness gate before the first solicitation
workflow.description: Check every pass condition with its evidence and date; block the class of business governed by any condition that cannot pass
workflow.artifact: signed readiness checklist with evidence dates and any blocked classes named
workflow.gate: every condition is evidenced and dated, no condition is waived, and each failed condition is recorded with the class of business it currently blocks

priority_rationale: Authority comes first because nothing else in a property and casualty agency is lawful without it: the charter fixes what is being licensed for, the individual and entity licenses and the appointments create the right to act, and errors-and-omissions coverage and the binding grant bound how that right may be used. The agency-model and carrier-access work sits next because ownership of expirations, commission mechanics and the access path chosen determine whether the business being written is an asset or someone else's book. Market focus, line economics and referral architecture follow, since they only make sense once the agency knows what it may write and through whom, and the conduct and readiness units close the order because they govern the first consumer contact and gate everything upstream before a single policy is sold.

dominance_rules.rule: Licensing and appointment authority dominates every sales opportunity
dominance_rules.rationale: soliciting, quoting or binding without the individual license, the entity license where required, and an in-force appointment exposes the agency to regulatory action, can void the transaction and can forfeit compensation, and no account is worth that outcome
dominance_rules.trigger: a prospect, referral or renewal appears in a state or for a carrier where authority is not confirmed in force
dominance_rules.action: do not solicit, quote or bind; obtain the authority first or refer the risk to a properly licensed producer and record the referral

dominance_rules.rule: Carrier-determined pricing dominates any savings message
dominance_rules.rationale: premium and eligibility are produced by carrier rating and underwriting, so a savings promise is a claim the agency has no power to keep and sets up both the client and the agency to be harmed
dominance_rules.trigger: any script, advertisement, proposal or conversation that states or implies the consumer will pay less, that a quote will hold, or that coverage is in place
dominance_rules.action: replace it with an offer to shop and to explain how carriers set premium, and confirm coverage only when the carrier has confirmed it

dominance_rules.rule: Documented client fit dominates commission, contingency and split economics
dominance_rules.rationale: compensation differences between carriers are real and recurring, and an agency that lets them decide placements will eventually place a client badly and be unable to explain why
dominance_rules.trigger: the best-paying market for a risk is not the best-serving one, or a carrier's contingency threshold is within reach
dominance_rules.action: place on the documented comparison of coverage, claims handling, financial strength and price, and record the reason for the carrier chosen in the file

dominance_rules.rule: Ownership of expirations and exit terms dominate headline compensation when choosing a model or a group
dominance_rules.rationale: the renewal book is the agency's asset, and a contract that conditions or forfeits it converts years of work into someone else's property regardless of what the split paid meanwhile
dominance_rules.trigger: any offer that pairs attractive compensation with restrictive termination, covenant or appointment-name terms
dominance_rules.action: answer the ownership, termination and exit questions from the written clauses first and decline or renegotiate before compensation is discussed

dominance_rules.rule: Written binding authority dominates client urgency
dominance_rules.rationale: a placement made outside the grant may not be honoured, and the client who believes they are covered is the person who pays for that, with the agency's errors-and-omissions exposure behind it
dominance_rules.trigger: a deadline, a favour or a system that appears to permit binding a risk outside the written grant or during a suspension event
dominance_rules.action: refer it to the underwriter with the deadline stated, tell the client in writing that coverage is not in force until the carrier confirms, and offer the wholesale or surplus-lines route instead

dominance_rules.rule: Written contract language dominates verbal assurance from a recruiter, marketer or field representative
dominance_rules.rationale: the people describing an opportunity are rarely the people who will administer the termination clause, and only the signed document is enforceable
dominance_rules.trigger: any material term - compensation, ownership, appointment name, exit, production minimum - described verbally but absent from or contradicted by the agreement
dominance_rules.action: require it in the document before signing, and treat its absence as the actual answer

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure-first identification dominates any marketing response-rate argument
dominance_rules.rationale: a contact that obscures who is calling and why taints everything that follows and is the origin of most conduct complaints in this business
dominance_rules.trigger: any script, mailer, landing page or vendor approach that hides or softens the insurance purpose or the agency's identity
dominance_rules.action: rewrite it to open with the agency's name, its licensed status, whether it represents one carrier or several, and the purpose of the contact, or do not use it

dominance_rules.rule: Vulnerable-consumer care dominates closing the sale
dominance_rules.rationale: a decision taken by a consumer who did not understand it is not a sale the agency can defend, and disaster, age, language and literacy pressures are exactly when insurance decisions get made badly
dominance_rules.trigger: signs of disaster stress, confusion, cognitive difficulty, limited English or limited literacy in a consumer conversation
dominance_rules.action: slow down, provide a written summary, welcome a family member or trusted adviser, remove every urgency that is not a real deadline, and stop if understanding is not present

dominance_rules.rule: Verified current jurisdiction and carrier rules dominate remembered or second-hand answers
dominance_rules.rationale: licensing, appointment, fee, rebating and advertising requirements differ by state and by carrier and change, so an answer that was right last year or in another state is not evidence
dominance_rules.trigger: any compliance question answered from memory, from a peer, from a vendor's marketing, or from another state's practice
dominance_rules.action: verify with the state insurance department, the carrier's own agreement, or counsel, and record the source and date of the answer

dominance_rules.rationale: accounts written past capacity produce the missed endorsements and unanswered requests that become both lost renewals and errors-and-omissions claims, so unserviceable growth destroys the asset it appears to build
dominance_rules.trigger: new business would take the agency past its written account capacity, or an appointment would be accepted that the agency cannot feed or learn
dominance_rules.action: hold at capacity or decline the appointment until staffing, systems or process measurably change what the agency can carry

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the individual license, the entity license and the carrier and state appointment before quoting anything in that state or for that carrier
anti_rework_rules.prevents: solicitation without authority, voided or unpaid business, and a regulatory exposure no later correction removes

anti_rework_rules.rule: Bind errors-and-omissions coverage before signing carrier or group agreements, and never break the retroactive date afterwards
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a contracting packet that stalls for missing evidence, and a coverage gap that strands every placement made before the new policy

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose the market focus before selecting carriers, systems or paying for a single lead
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a carrier shelf, an appetite map, a rating system and a lead budget built for a segment the agency does not actually serve

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read and abstract ownership of expirations, termination, covenant and assignment clauses before signing any carrier, group or employment agreement
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a renewal book the agency does not own, cannot move and cannot sell, discovered only when it tries to leave

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify what each access path requires - experience, capital, volume, coverage limits, minimums - before promising a carrier or a group anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a contracting application that fails on a known disqualifier, and production commitments the chosen market cannot honestly produce

anti_rework_rules.rule: Model commission timing, settlement path and reversal behaviour before committing to any fixed cost
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cash crunch mid-build caused by treating written premium as collected revenue and ignoring return commission

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map carrier appetite for the intended niche, with a primary and a backup market, before marketing into it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a pipeline of risks nobody on the shelf will write and a marketing spend that has to be abandoned

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear every referral compensation arrangement against rebating, inducement and settlement-service rules before any money or gift moves
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinding a productive relationship under regulatory pressure and the complaint history that comes with it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Enter each obligation into the calendar with its lead time at the moment it is first incurred, not at its first renewal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a lapsed license, entity registration, appointment or coverage that stops production and must be reported on every future application

anti_rework_rules.rule: Standardize the disclosure-first script and the documentation template before the first prospect contact
anti_rework_rules.prevents: inconsistent early files and contact records that later have to be defended one by one in a complaint or an errors-and-omissions claim

iteration_protocol.trigger: a carrier restricts a class, withdraws from a territory, imposes a moratorium or issues a non-renewal programme affecting a core line
iteration_protocol.action: pause marketing into the affected class, re-run the appetite map for a primary and a backup home including wholesale routes, and confirm the access plan still covers every line in the charter

iteration_protocol.trigger: a carrier issues a production warning, a loss-ratio concern, a restriction or a run-off notice
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure the agency's own placed volume, retention and loss signal against the agreement, decide whether the appointment can honestly be fed, and re-check the written concentration limit before reacting

iteration_protocol.trigger: an errors-and-omissions claim, notice of circumstance or near-miss occurs
iteration_protocol.action: report it as the policy requires, trace the failure to the binding grant, the documentation habit or the service load that produced it, and change that mechanism rather than the individual file

iteration_protocol.trigger: a group, franchise or wholesale partner changes its fees, contingency treatment, appointment arrangements or exit terms
iteration_protocol.action: re-abstract the agreement, re-price the access against the direct-appointment alternative and the written exit cost, and decide whether to renegotiate, cap the share of the book placed there, or leave

iteration_protocol.trigger: a state is added to the footprint, or a client's risk turns out to sit in a state the agency does not serve
iteration_protocol.action: run the nonresident licensing, carrier authorization and appointment checks for that state, add its obligations to the calendar, and until all three clear, refer the risk and record it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a regulatory or carrier rule change is published in an operating state touching licensing, education, fees, advertising, contact or privacy
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the affected obligation class with the department or the carrier, update the calendar and the contact standard, and record the source and date of the answer

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured service touches per account drift outside the recorded band, or account count approaches the written capacity
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure per-line touch counts, recompute capacity, and hold new business at the ceiling until staffing, systems or process change the measurement

iteration_protocol.trigger: a channel's measured cost per bound account drifts outside its band, or a source begins producing contacts with a doubtful consent basis
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure the channel stage by stage to find which rate moved, re-verify the consent basis and the compensation arrangement, and retire the channel rather than repair a message that cannot be made honest

iteration_protocol.trigger: commission statements stop reconciling, or a contingency statement arrives materially different from the modelled expectation
iteration_protocol.action: reconcile the statement against the recorded rate, base and settlement mechanism per carrier, correct the runway model's assumptions, and re-examine whether any placement pattern was bent toward a threshold
